shots.phrase: Begin by framing Introduction to Machine Learning Workflow as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
Machine-learning workflows separate data preparation, training, validation, testing, model selection, and evaluation.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Data Preparation and Leakage Prevention precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Preprocessing must be fitted only on permitted training data to avoid leakage.
Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them.
With the foundation in place, examine how Supervised vs.
Supervised methods learn a mapping from examples paired with target labels.
Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition.
Next, compare the choices involved in Statistical Analysis and Data Visualization and make the decision criteria explicit.

Topics include: Mathematical background of machine learning (for example statistical analysis and visualization of data), Bayesian decision theory, parametric and non-parameteric classification models (for example, SVMs and Nearest Neighbor models) and neural network models (for example Convolutional, Recurrent, and Deep Neural Networks).
Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts.
Apply Bayesian Decision Theory to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes work around Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Parametric Classification Models, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
An introduction to both foundational and modern machine learning theories and algorithms, and their application in classification and regression.
State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable.
Stress-test the reasoning around Non-Parametric Classification Models with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Unsupervised methods identify structure without target labels.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Neural Network Architectures to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Risk analysis considers data quality and uncertainty.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Model Evaluation and Hyperparameter Selection to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Evaluation metrics must match the task and the cost of different errors.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
It also considers robustness, privacy, security, transparency, and fairness.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
